Three of your four items are done and in the merge queue. #3773 is not done: a sound fix needs a design decision in the shared resolver.

| Issue | Outcome |
|---|---|
| #3844 | Closed as superseded, because the 2026-10-04 removal of the Go data-race analysis left nothing to report |
| #3835 part A | PR #4734 makes guards on an unconstrained parameter decided in contradictory-condition |
| #3835 part B | PR #4733 reports python-absent-member as "not run" when its Python declaration surface is missing |
| #3835 stopgap | bifrost-packs#67 makes python-absent-member opt-in until the engine change ships |
| #3840 | PR #4736 adds PHP include and require import edges and a diagnostic for dynamic targets |
| #3773 | Not landed; findings posted on the issue |

**#3835.** I posted your decision on the issue.
- **Part A.** Parameters now start as "unconstrained", separate from "information lost". Call results and field loads still count as lost. A repeated `x is None` guard is still proven contradictory.
- **Part B.** A default-selected policy that can't run does not change the exit status. A policy you name explicitly by ID that can't run still exits 2.
- **Schema change.** The report schema moves to version 6. The VS Code extension, now in bifrost-lsp, accepts only version 5, so I filed bifrost-lsp#11 for the matching change.

**#3840.** Static include paths become file edges for `importers-of` and `imports-of`. That covers literals, `__DIR__`, and `dirname(...)`. A non-static include path, such as a variable, now produces a structured incomplete diagnostic that lists the affected files. It is no longer silent. The change needs one migration and a PHP epoch bump.

**#3773 needs your call.** Removing the inactive cfg item does let the active import win. The answer still stays incomplete, because the inactive item's incompleteness reasons were already merged into shared reason sets that don't record their source. The lane's first fix removed every reason of the same kind. I rejected that, because it would also erase real, independent gaps. Two sound directions exist:
- **Narrow:** remove only reasons that carry a semantic ID inside the refuted item. Some reasons already carry one. Other reasons would keep the answer incomplete.
- **General:** record the source of each reason in the shared resolver. That code is the native-engine area other agents are working in.

The work is on an unpushed branch, and the lane is parked with its context.

**Also worth knowing:**
- **#3296 and #3192 stay open.** You asked on 2026-09-13 to keep #3296 open. David decided on 2026-10-06 to keep #3192 open for observation.
- **Four native-point tests fail locally on unmodified master.** Those tests normally run in per-push CI, but I did not check whether they fail there. They are listed on #3773.
- **Validation per PR:** focused tests, golden reviews, and Clippy on every touched crate after merging master. The local pack drift check fails identically on master because of one file's line endings, so CI is the real check there.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The #3773 problem is a common trap in sound analyzers. Once you merge incompleteness as a plain set of reason kinds, you can't later retract one source's contribution. Retraction needs provenance, either attached to each reason or implied by an ID the reason already carries.
- #3835 shows the same idea twice. "Unknown because the input is free" and "unknown because we lost track" must be separate states. So must "not run" and "ran but incomplete". Merging either pair makes the tool look less reliable than it is.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The general fix for #3773 is done, validated, and open as PR #4747. It is ready for the merge queue and depends on the #3840 PR, #4736, because each adds a cache migration and they must land in order.

**How the fix records where each reason came from.** I didn't add candidate tags to every place reasons are merged. The investigation showed that would not fix the bug. The reasons that kept the answer incomplete sit on the surviving candidate's path. They are the inner item's "may or may not exist" gaps, picked up while proving the outer binding isn't shadowed. Each such reason already has a unique identity built from the code site that produced it. The stored gap records link that site to the declaration it belongs to. So the source is recorded in the reason's identity and the existing tables, not in the merge code.

**What changed.**
- **Selection.** The shared selector removes winners whose cfg is known inactive, then selects again. Unknown cfg behaves as before.
- **Ownership lookup.** A new language hook maps a reason to the declaration that owns it. The default returns nothing. The Rust version is one SQL join, with a new index added by migration 0165 and query-plan tests.
- **Discharge rule.** The shared access step now drops a reason in two cases: its owning declaration is cfg-inactive for this reference, or the reason is that declaration's activation question and activation is decided. Matching is always by identity, never by kind.
- **Design chapter.** The evidence-and-results chapter states the rule. The ExecPlan I wrote for this work was deleted in the final commit, as the repo requires.

**Validation.**
- **Witnesses.** Both #3773 regression tests are un-ignored and pass.
- **Soundness controls.** Three new tests cover the cases that matter. An active local item still keeps its reason. Unknown cfg still stays incomplete. A refuted item's reason is removed while a reason of the same kind at a different declaration stays. That last case is the one the earlier kind-based attempt got wrong.
- **Suites.** The Rust usage suite passes 153 of 153 tests. That includes two tests that a filter-only version broke and that were first confirmed to pass on master. Schema and migration tests, the query-plan tests, and Clippy on the analysis and core crates also pass.

**Today's other changes, all in the queue:**

| PR | Change |
|---|---|
| #4733 | Report a default policy that lacks its workspace capability as "not run" |
| #4734 | Count a guard on an unconstrained parameter as decided |
| #4736 | Add PHP include/require import edges |
| #4747 | Stop a cfg-refuted Rust local from hiding the active binding |
| bifrost-packs#67 | Make the Python absent-member policy opt-in as a stopgap |

**Still open.**
- **bifrost-lsp#11.** The VS Code extension still accepts only report schema 5. It needs updating before an engine release that includes #4733.
- **Four native-point tests fail locally on unmodified master.** I did not check whether CI fails them too. They are listed on #3773 and in the PR.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Tracking where a reason came from does not always mean threading tags through every merge. If each reason already has a unique identity tied to its site, a join after the fact recovers the owner exactly, and the hot merge code stays unchanged.
- "Remove the losing candidate's reasons" sounds like a fix but is the wrong question. The leftover reasons belonged to the winner's proof that it was not shadowed. The right question was which declaration each reason is about, not which path carried it.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
